title: The dharma you're skipping (Bhagavad Gita)
description:
It's eleven at night. You're on your phone. A friend just got promoted. An old classmate is suddenly engaged. And you feel... behind.

Two thousand three hundred years ago, on the edge of a battlefield, the Gita described this exactly. Chapter 3, verse 35: "Better is one's own dharma, though imperfectly performed, than the dharma of another, well performed."

This video is about why comparison breaks — and one specific practice for this week to break the back of it.

Source: Bhagavad Gita, chapter 3, verse 35. Translation by Eknath Easwaran (public domain).

The practice:
1. Sit down somewhere quiet — Sunday night or Monday morning.
2. Write down ONE task for this season (the next three months).
3. Measure only against that. When you catch yourself looking sideways, bring your eyes back to the page.

One page. One task. One season. Stay on your road.

Chariot of the Self — ancient Indian wisdom (Gita, Upanishads, Yoga Sutras, Chanakya) turned into practices for the modern mind. Not religion. The oldest operating manual for the human mind, still running.
